decisions.title: JSON files in git are the single source of truth
decisions.body: All project data lives exclusively in versioned files in the repo: /registry/**.json, /sources/sources.json, /decisions/decisions.json, /dossiers/**, /docs/**.md. No databases, no data inside components, no external stores at baseline. Versioning, review, and status history come from git itself. Escalation away from files happens only when the triggers in docs/architecture.md fire (corpora arrive, >500 implementations, etc.).

decisions.title: /cards are generated projections, never hand-edited
decisions.body: Human-readable mechanism cards in /cards/{id}.md are output only, rendered from registry JSON by tools/render-cards.ts (npm run cards). They are never created or edited by hand; any change to a card goes through its source record in /registry/mechanisms and a regeneration. This keeps exactly one editable representation of each mechanism.

decisions.title: A mechanism without metrics or hard constraints is invalid
decisions.body: A full L1 record must have non-empty implementations[].metrics and non-empty constraints.hard_rules, otherwise the validator rejects it. Rationale: a mechanism we cannot measure is not knowledge, and a mechanism without guardrails is a dark-pattern risk. The schema is not weakened for convenience; seed stubs use a separate reduced sub-schema in /registry/mechanisms/_seed/ instead.

decisions.title: Core roster is seed v0.9 — candidates until dossiers pass
decisions.body: The 12-mechanism roster (LA-01 plus 11 stubs) is a seed hypothesis, not a settled core. All stubs carry lifecycle_status 'candidate' and contain only id, name, grade_draft, oneliner, parent. Promotion to incubating/core happens exclusively through scored dossiers (5 axes, thresholds per /dossiers/dossier.schema.json), entered by the owner or the future derivation pipeline — never by fleshing out stubs in code.

decisions.title: Showcase honesty contract: every status computed from files on disk
decisions.body: Every status shown in the Control Center (live / in progress / planned, counts, coverage) is computed at render time from actual data files. Hardcoding a status or a number in JSX/TS is forbidden. Where no data exists yet, the UI shows a designed empty state naming the file or pipeline that will fill it and the phase. The showcase may never look more finished than the shelves actually are.

decisions.title: Single-password auth via HMAC cookie and middleware
decisions.body: Auth per SPEC §5: middleware.ts guards all routes except /login and static assets. /login posts to a server action that compares the submitted password against env ACCESS_PASSWORD (constant-time) and, on success, sets an httpOnly cookie 'me_session' containing '<expiresAtMs>.<hmac>' signed with HMAC-SHA256(env SESSION_SECRET), maxAge 30 days, sameSite lax, secure in production. In-memory sliding-window rate limit: 5 attempts/min per IP (x-forwarded-for), resets on server restart — acceptable at baseline (single instance). No auth libraries; Web Crypto in middleware (Edge) and node:crypto timingSafeEqual in the action. No accounts, roles, OAuth, session DB, or analytics. IDs D-001–D-005 are reserved for the owner-specified baseline decisions (SPEC §3.5).

decisions.title: Hosting on Vercel with git-connected auto-deploy from main
decisions.body: Deployed to Vercel (project motivation-engine, personal scope), production URL https://motivation-engine-pi.vercel.app. GitHub repo itrunov7/motivation-engine is connected, so every push to main auto-deploys to production and every later step is verified live. Env vars ACCESS_PASSWORD and SESSION_SECRET are set as sensitive values in Production and Preview environments; the production SESSION_SECRET is freshly generated and distinct from the local dev secret, and the production ACCESS_PASSWORD replaces the dev placeholder. No custom domain, no additional infrastructure — file-based baseline runs as-is on Vercel serverless.

decisions.title: Tooling stack: tsx + Ajv for validator and card generator
decisions.body: tools/validate.ts and tools/render-cards.ts run via tsx (npm run validate / npm run cards) — no build step for tooling. Validation uses Ajv 2020-12 (ajv + ajv-formats) against the JSON schemas in the repo; the hard rule (non-empty implementations[].metrics and constraints.hard_rules, D-003) is additionally enforced by an explicit check in validate.ts so it fails loudly even if the schema were ever weakened. taxonomy.json, sources.json, and decisions.json are validated against inline schemas mirroring SPEC §3.1/§3.4/§3.5; dossier.schema.json is compiled for integrity and any future dossier records are validated against it including total = sum of axis scores. CI (.github/workflows/validate.yml) runs install, validate, and build on every push, so invalid knowledge physically cannot enter the repo.

decisions.title: Status computation centralized in lib/status.ts
decisions.body: All showcase block statuses (live / in progress / planned) are computed in a single server-only module, lib/status.ts — the only file in the codebase where status literals may appear; components map presentation through STATUS_META keys, never through literals. Rules per SPEC §4: Registry is live when at least one full record passes the hard rules (non-empty implementations[].metrics and constraints.hard_rules, D-003); Schema & validator when the schema files and the CI workflow exist; Card generator when /cards holds a generated {id}.md for a valid full record. Folder-driven blocks (runtime, corpora, telemetry) treat README.md, dotfiles, .gitkeep, and empty subfolders as non-data, and a corpus subfolder counts only when named after a source id from sources.json and containing a manifest.json (per the /corpora contract) — so an empty or fake folder can never turn a block green. Typed data loaders live in lib/data.ts and are reused by later showcase pages.

decisions.title: Docs render via react-markdown; /sources filters via URL searchParams
decisions.body: The remaining showcase pages stay Server Components end to end. /docs/[slug] renders the five foundation documents with react-markdown + remark-gfm (the first runtime dependencies beyond Next itself) — server-compatible, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML, GFM tables supported; slugs are allowlisted in lib/data.ts (DOC_SLUGS) and unknown slugs 404. /sources filters (class A–D, priority P0–P2, status) are plain links that toggle URL searchParams and the table is filtered server-side — zero client JS, shareable filter URLs. /dossiers reads /dossiers/*.json via loadDossiers() (excluding the schema), so its empty state is computed from the folder being empty, never asserted; source status presentation lives in SOURCE_STATUS_META in lib/status.ts, keeping status literals out of app/ (D-005, D-009).

decisions.title: Constitution amendment: controlled external-API whitelist for tools/ scripts (Phase 2)
decisions.body: Baseline forbade all external fetches (former rule 12 in .cursorrules). Phase 2 opens a controlled whitelist: scripts under tools/ MAY call exactly four public APIs — api.openalex.org, api.semanticscholar.org, PubMed E-utilities (eutils.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov), and web.archive.org (CDX API). Any other external endpoint requires a new decisions.json entry first. The Next.js app remains file-based with zero runtime external calls from app/ (including middleware and server actions); data reading stays fs-only. LLM API calls remain forbidden everywhere in the repo. General scrapers stay forbidden; source connectors exist only as tools/ scripts against the whitelisted APIs.

decisions.title: Connector framework: one contract, one runner, one manifest shape, 40 MB corpus guardrail
decisions.body: All source connectors implement a single Connector interface (tools/connectors/types.ts) and are executed only through tools/run-connector.ts (npm run connector -- <id> [key=value ...]). Every run — success, partial, or failed — writes /corpora/{source_id}/manifest.json: { source_id, connector_version, last_run {timestamp, status, params, records_fetched, files_written, duration_s, error?}, run_history (last 20 runs, newest first), data_files [{path, records, bytes}] }, so corpus statuses in the showcase stay computed from disk. Shared helpers bake the guardrails in rather than trusting each connector: fetch is rate-limited with 3 attempts and exponential backoff, sends polite User-Agent/mailto headers, and hard-rejects any host outside the D-011 whitelist; JSON output is pretty-printed for reviewable git diffs. Guardrail: a corpus directory exceeding 40 MB fails the run with a message pointing at the Postgres escalation trigger in docs/architecture.md (corpora at thousands-of-rows scale move to managed Postgres / object storage; the repo is never silently bloated). Connectors with a "_"-prefixed source_id (e.g. the dummy smoke-test connector) are internal and ignored by the showcase. The validator checks every corpus manifest against this contract.

decisions.title: Source connection modes and manifest-derived statuses; app-store-reviews source added
decisions.body: "0/30 connected" was a false metric — it conflated four different source natures under one connectivity claim. Every source in sources.json now carries connection_mode: api (automated connector), report (one-off ingested artifact), manual (licensed human curation, never machine-harvested), or deferred (P2, not planned this phase; optional mode_note records why). The stored status field is removed entirely: states are computed in lib/status.ts from /corpora/{source_id}/manifest.json — an api source is connected iff last_run.status = "success"; a report source is ingested iff additionally at least one data_files entry exists on disk; manual and deferred sources show their mode, never a fake connectivity status. Owner assignment: api = openalex, semantic-scholar, pubmed-europepmc, wayback-cdx, sec-edgar, google-patents, app-store-reviews (7); report = revenuecat-report, unbounce-benchmarks, product-analytics-benchmarks, goodui, forrt (5); manual = mobbin, screensdesign, pageflows, paywall-galleries, growth-design, built-for-mars, gdc, baymard, engineering-blogs (9); deferred = appstore-screenshot-history, psyarxiv-osf, metabus, psychopen-cama, cochrane, neurosynth, neurovault, sensor-tower, ftc-eu-enforcement, company-handbooks (10). New owner-provided source app-store-reviews (App Store / Google Play review texts as emotional labels, class C, P1, api mode, $0 via public APIs / RSS feeds) is a distinct source from appstore-screenshot-history, which is deferred pending a paid-subscription purchase decision. No ad-libraries source is added — that is a September buy-vs-build decision with its own record. sec-edgar and google-patents record api intent, but their endpoints are outside the D-011 whitelist; building those connectors requires a new decision first. /sources and Overview group by mode: api n/7 connected · report n/5 ingested · manual 9 curation · deferred 10.

decisions.title: Connectors decoupled from sources: manifest source_ids[] declares what a corpus harvests
decisions.body: A connector is not a source. The first real connector (evidence) harvests two registry sources — openalex and semantic-scholar — into one merged corpus /corpora/evidence/{mechanism_id}.json, which the D-013 rule (corpus dir name = source id) cannot express without dishonest states: either a fake "evidence" source record in sources.json, or marking actively-harvested real sources deferred. The manifest contract gains one field: source_ids: string[] — the sources.json ids the corpus harvests (empty for "_"-prefixed internal corpora). Status computation in lib/status.ts changes to: an api source is connected iff ANY /corpora/{dir}/manifest.json lists it in source_ids with last_run.status = "success"; a report source is ingested iff additionally that corpus has a data_files entry on disk. Corpus dir names no longer need to match source ids; the validator instead checks that every source_ids entry exists in sources.json and that non-internal corpora harvest at least one source. This future-proofs the framework: the wayback connector will list source_ids: ["wayback-cdx"], and any future connector serving multiple sources (e.g. one benchmarks ingester covering several report sources) works without new registry entities.

decisions.title: Evidence terms live in mechanism records; corpus must be able to disconfirm
decisions.body: Search terms for the evidence connector are per-mechanism DATA, not hardcoded CLI params. The mechanism schema (full records) gains an optional evidence_terms: string[]; the connector reads terms from the record, falling back to [name] for records without the field (an explicit terms= param still overrides for ad-hoc runs). Rationale: generic terms harvest only confirming mainstream literature; dissent, replication, and boundary-condition papers require targeted terms — a corpus that can only confirm is methodologically broken. LA-01's owner-provided terms therefore include 'loss aversion replication', 'loss aversion moderators', 'loss of loss aversion', and 'loss aversion small stakes' alongside the mainstream ones. Second change: deduplication now unions DOI AND normalized title (lowercase, punctuation and asterisks stripped) into transitive clusters and keeps the highest-citation variant of each paper, instead of first-seen-wins by DOI only. Connector bumped to v1.1.0 (output gained terms_source and terms).

decisions.title: Internal connection mode; four owner-provided sources added (ventora-telemetry, failure-postmortems, email-flow-galleries, cultural-ux-variation)
decisions.body: The connection_mode vocabulary (D-013) gains a fifth value: internal — data produced by our own platform, not an external source. An internal source proves connectivity the same way an api source does: connected iff any /corpora/{dir}/manifest.json lists it in source_ids with last_run.status = "success"; no status is ever stored. Four owner-provided sources enter sources.json: ventora-telemetry (class C, P0, internal — Amplitude events from Ventora-built products carrying mechanism_tags, the only source that fills observed_effects and promotes mechanisms to CORE), failure-postmortems (class D, P2, manual — the anti-survivorship corpus of startup autopsies and failed-product teardowns), email-flow-galleries (class A, P2, manual — lifecycle email and push-sequence libraries covering artifact types screen libraries miss), and cultural-ux-variation (class B, P2, deferred — geo/cultural variation of interface surfaces, a placeholder keeping the gap visible). The access enum grows by the four exact access strings; the vocabulary stays closed. tools/connectors/wayback-domains.json gains a dead_products section (empty, owner-filled) so the anti-survivorship track has a slot in the interface-evolution corpus. Rationale: Ventora telemetry deferred to September — no engineering capacity; M3 live test moves to the team integration phase.

decisions.title: Connector harvests breadth; owner pins the tail — 100% recall is a human+machine contract, not a query-tuning goal
decisions.body: The evidence connector cannot surface every paper that matters for a dossier: citation-sorted search and finite per-term caps systematically miss low-citation boundary-condition and dissent works even after targeted evidence_terms (D-015). Full records gain an optional pinned_evidence: [{title, doi, reason}] array — owner-authored by hand. The connector merges pinned entries into /corpora/evidence/{mechanism_id}.json with source_api: "pinned", fetching metadata from OpenAlex by DOI (falling back to the owner title/doi if the lookup fails). Dedup still unions DOI and normalized title; when a pin overlaps a harvested record the pin wins source_api so the owner's intent stays visible. Rationale: chasing 100% recall by query-tuning is a false goal; the honest contract is breadth from the connector plus a human-pinned tail. LA-01 pins two dossier-cited boundary papers (Ert & Erev 2013 small-stakes; Walasek & Stewart 2015 disappear-and-reverse).

decisions.title: Semantic Scholar authentication and graceful keyless degradation in the evidence connector
decisions.body: The evidence connector reads an optional S2_API_KEY env var and sends it as the x-api-key header — authenticated Semantic Scholar clients get materially higher rate limits than the shared keyless pool, which 429s in bursts and made full-success runs a lottery. Keyless degradation: on the first HTTP 429 without a key the run flips into throttled mode instead of failing — per-term batch drops from 15 to 10 for the retry passes, retry cooldowns become exponential (30s, 60s, 120s), and the manifest run entry records warnings: { s2_throttled: true }. The manifest contract (D-012) gains the optional warnings field (object of booleans) for connector degradation flags; the validator accepts it. CI: the validate workflow passes S2_API_KEY from the repository secret of the same name (empty when unset — connectors degrade gracefully); local usage is documented in the tools/ runbook. No behavior change otherwise — we are already API-only; this is authentication, not architecture. Connector bumped to v1.3.0.

decisions.title: Corpus completeness is verified structurally — review-reference coverage and category checklist — not by knowing the answers in advance
decisions.body: Evidence connector v2 (2.0.0) adds two structural completeness checks that need no ground truth. (1) Snowballing: after the term harvest, review/meta-analysis records are identified from the OpenAlex type field plus title keywords (meta-analysis / systematic review); for the top 2 by citations, their referenced_works are fetched from OpenAlex, coverage = the share of each review's resolved references already in the corpus, and references missing from the corpus that appear in ≥2 reviews' lists are auto-added with source_api "snowball". The coverage_report (per-review references_total / references_resolved / references_in_corpus / coverage, plus snowball_added) is written into the evidence file. (2) Category checklist: every record is classified into the non-exclusive categories foundational (≥1000 citations), meta-analysis (type/title), replication (title/abstract markers), dissent (documented disconfirmation markers in title/abstract/pin_reason), and recent (≤5 years old) — metadata only, the connector never judges scientific content. Records gain openalex_id, openalex_type, and categories; per-category counts go into the evidence file (category_counts) and the corpus manifest (data_files[].categories). The new /connectors cockpit renders the checklist per data file and flags any empty category red; red (#F87171) enters lib/status.ts as the one deliberate alert-token addition to the palette, for structural gaps and failed runs. Validator rule: a dossier referencing a mechanism whose evidence file is missing, unclassified, or has an empty dissent category FAILS — a corpus that can only confirm is broken.

decisions.title: Corpus manifest contract is locked in CI — validator schema key-derived from the connector contract, writer pinned to reader at compile time
decisions.body: Triggered by a production incident investigation: openalex and semantic-scholar showed not_connected on the deployed Control Center. The trace ruled out every structural suspect — corpora/evidence/manifest.json is tracked in main (no .gitignore exclusion), it validates against the manifest contract (source_ids present, last_run present), and the Vercel production deployment was built from the exact main HEAD sha. Root cause: the last committed connector run had status "partial" (all Semantic Scholar queries hit keyless HTTP 429, D-018), and computeSourceState treats a source as connected only when a manifest lists it in source_ids with last_run.status "success" — run_history successes do not count, and the corpus-level status flips ALL sources the corpus harvests, so OpenAlex went red alongside Semantic Scholar despite succeeding in that same run. The showcase honestly rendered degraded data; no code defect. But the investigation exposed a real latent risk: the manifest contract exists in three hand-maintained mirrors — writer (tools/connectors/types.ts Manifest), reader (lib/types.ts CorpusManifest, which lib/status.ts computes source states from; lib never imports tools), and the Ajv schema inside tools/validate.ts. A connector refactor could change the written shape, update one mirror, and validation would stay green while statuses silently flipped. Guard added in tools/validate.ts: (1) the Ajv schema's properties and required keys are now derived from the writer contract via TypeScript satisfies constraints (Record<keyof Manifest, unknown> etc.) — a field renamed, removed, or added without a schema update no longer compiles; (2) a type-level assertion pins Manifest to CorpusManifest, so the writer can never stop satisfying what status computation reads; (3) manifest discovery is now recursive — every /corpora/**/manifest.json at any depth is validated, with internal ("_"-prefixed) dirs recognized at any level. Both npm run validate and the type check inside npm run build run in CI on every push, so contract drift turns the build red instead of flipping sources to not_connected on production. The incident status itself needs no code fix: a success run (reliable with S2_API_KEY, D-018) restores connected; per-source run granularity remains a possible future refinement of D-014.

decisions.title: Health is a separate axis from connection — a 6-hourly heartbeat file, probes restricted to the D-011 whitelist, stale renders unknown
decisions.body: Connection (computed from corpus manifests, D-013/D-014: has a harvest run ever succeeded) says nothing about whether an API is answering right now, so the two are now independent axes. tools/health-check.ts (npm run health) performs ONE minimal single-record request per probeable api source — one attempt, no retries, because retries would mask throttling — and writes /corpora/_health/heartbeat.json ({generated_at, entries[]: {source_id, checked_at, status, latency_ms, note}}). Status mapping: ok = 2xx; degraded = HTTP 429/206 (the s2_throttled condition, D-018); down = network error, timeout, or 5xx. Probes are restricted to the D-011 whitelist: openalex, semantic-scholar, pubmed-europepmc, wayback-cdx get probes; app-store-reviews, sec-edgar, google-patents get status unknown with a no-probe note — the whitelist grows when a connector for a source actually gets built, not ahead of it (probing hosts we do not harvest is surface without purpose). ventora-telemetry (internal) is n_a — no external endpoint by design; unknown would read as a problem. Scheduling: .github/workflows/connectors.yml runs the check every 6 hours plus workflow_dispatch and commits (data: prefix) only when git sees a diff. Commit-noise rule, resolved in the script rather than the workflow: the file is rewritten only when the per-source status vector changed OR the committed heartbeat is older than 11 hours — the 11h refresh keeps a quiet heartbeat inside the UI's 12h stale threshold at ~2 commits/day worst case. UI: /sources and /connectors render two independent indicators per api/internal source — connection (from manifests, unchanged) and health (from the heartbeat, with checked-Nh-ago); a heartbeat older than 12h renders as unknown, never as ok. The app performs NO live external calls — health is read from the heartbeat file only (constitution invariant 12 stands: no runtime external fetches from app/). Contract safety mirrors D-020: lib/types.ts carries the reader (HeartbeatFile), tools/health-check.ts the writer, and tools/validate.ts pins writer to reader with an AssertAssignable guard plus a key-derived Ajv schema validated when the file is present; every entry's source_id must exist in sources.json. A down source is a recorded fact, not a script failure — the script exits non-zero only on script errors. Runbook (tools/README.md): connected+down = wait/retry later; connected+degraded = check rate limits/keys; not_connected+ok = no successful harvest run exists — run the connector.

decisions.title: Operations completion — a manifest cost block, a monthly cockpit rollup, and retry-then-issue failure automation; the operator watches issues, not logs
decisions.body: Closes the operations loop on top of the D-021 heartbeat. (1) Cost accounting: every ManifestRun gains an optional cost block { api_calls, duration_s, tokens_in, tokens_out, estimated_usd } (tools/connectors/types.ts, mirrored in lib/types.ts CorpusManifestCost). api_calls is counted at the polite-fetch layer (tools/connectors/lib/http.ts now returns { fetch, stats } and increments on every outbound attempt INCLUDING retries — the honest request cost), duration_s mirrors the run duration, and estimated_usd is COMPUTED, not asserted: the D-011 whitelist is entirely free public APIs so a pure-fetch run computes to 0, and it becomes non-zero only when a priced job reports token usage. tokens_in/tokens_out are RESERVED for future LLM jobs and written null until an engine exists (invariant 5: no engine, no LLM calls this phase). cost is optional on the run because runs recorded before D-022 carry no block and rewriting history would be dishonest — the runner (tools/run-connector.ts) always writes it going forward. The validator schema is key-derived from ManifestCost via satisfies (same D-020 drift guard: all five keys required inside the block, tokens typed integer-or-null, additionalProperties false), so the writer, reader, and Ajv schema stay pinned at compile time. (2) Monthly rollup: lib/status.ts computeMonthlyRollup aggregates each manifest's run_history for the current UTC calendar month into per-connector rows plus a total (runs, api_calls, duration, estimated_usd); runs with no cost block contribute 0 to the money/call figures but still count as runs. The /connectors cockpit renders a MonthlyRollupPanel above the corpus panels with an honest empty state and the caveat that run_history is capped at RUN_HISTORY_LIMIT (20) per connector, so the rollup covers retained runs only. No number or status is hardcoded — everything is derived from manifests. (3) Failure automation: .github/workflows/connectors.yml retries a failed run once after a 60s backoff; on persistent failure it opens a GitHub issue titled connector:{id} failing, labeled ops, with the captured error output, then fails the run red. The ops label is created if missing, and creation is deduplicated by exact title among open ops issues — never a second issue while one is open; closing the issue after a fix re-arms the automation. The step is written generically around CONNECTOR_ID (today the health job, id health; a future scheduled harvest job reuses it verbatim and would paste last_run.error). The workflow uses the standard Actions token (issues: write) — no new external endpoint, so invariant 12 (which governs tools/ scripts) is untouched and no LLM calls are introduced. (4) Runbook (tools/README.md, Operations section): the operator's contract is watch issues, not logs — a green issue tracker means healthy operations; nobody reads Actions logs proactively.

decisions.title: Constitution amendment: a narrow git-backed write surface for the Operations UI
decisions.body: The app was strictly read-only (rule 12: no runtime external fetches from app/, including server actions; rule: no data-editing forms in the UI). This amendment opens a deliberately NARROW write surface so a non-technical operator can run the fleet without touching git. The rules change in three exact ways. (1) rule 1 (source of truth) now lists /corpora/_ops/**.json as operational config that the app MAY write; all other data — registry, dossiers, docs, sources, and decisions except the auto-entries below — stays read-only in the UI and is edited only in git. (2) rule 12 gains ONE external-fetch exception: server actions under app/ops/ MAY call api.github.com to (a) commit the allowlisted _ops write surface via the Contents API, (b) dispatch harvest workflows via workflow_dispatch, (c) poll a run, and (d) download a run's quote artifact — nothing else. The app never harvests; it only triggers the GitHub workflow that does. All other app/ code remains file-based with zero runtime external calls, and LLM API calls remain forbidden everywhere. (3) the no-UI-forms rule gains the same narrow exception. Enforcement is not by convention: every write funnels through one server-action guard with a hard allowlist — the exact path corpora/_ops/budget.json, or corpora/_ops/connectors/{id}.json where {id} matches ^[a-z0-9-]+$ AND is a registered connector, plus a single append-only operation on decisions/decisions.json that may only add a well-formed auto-entry (next D-XXX id, area operations). Any other path throws before a byte leaves the process. Auth is unchanged (D-006): the whole app, /ops included, sits behind the single-password middleware. The write token is a fine-grained, repo-scoped GitHub PAT read from env GH_OPS_TOKEN (never committed); without it the /ops page renders read-only with an honest empty state and every control disabled. Overrides (raising a cap for one run) are themselves logged: the same action appends an auto-entry to decisions.json, so the decision log stays the single source of truth for deviations — a cap was raised is a decision, not a silent flag.

decisions.title: Operational config lives in /corpora/_ops — budget caps and per-connector limits/pause/cadence/targets, validated in CI
decisions.body: The fleet's operating parameters become data, not code or hidden defaults. /corpora/_ops/budget.json holds { monthly_caps: { usd, calls } } — the ceiling the scheduler respects before starting new runs. /corpora/_ops/connectors/{id}.json holds, per connector, { connector_id, paused, paused_reason, cadence { every_days }, limits { max_calls_per_run, max_records_per_run }, targets[] }. targets is the explicit list the machine harvests (for evidence, mechanism ids) — the schedule's scope is what the owner pointed it at, not an accident of which files already exist on disk; it defaults to every mechanism id with a full record in /registry/mechanisms (currently LA-01), and the scheduled run applies a freshness filter on top (a target is only harvested if its registry record changed in the last 7 days, checked via git log). paused connectors are skipped by the scheduled workflow with the stored reason written to the job summary. The _ops directory is _-prefixed so it is ignored by the showcase corpus scan (lib/status.ts) exactly like _health and _dummy. Contract safety mirrors D-020/D-021: the writer/reader types live in tools/connectors/types.ts and lib/types.ts with an AssertAssignable drift guard in tools/validate.ts, and a SINGLE set of validators in lib/ops.ts is shared by both CI (npm run validate) and the server-action write path — so the UI can never push a config that would redden CI. Validation is strict: required fields, non-negative numbers, filename must equal connector_id, connector_id must be a registered connector, and every target must exist in /registry/mechanisms. Malformed _ops config fails the build rather than silently misconfiguring the fleet.

decisions.title: Run-with-quote flow: dry-run dispatch estimates cost before a real run; over-budget requires a logged override
decisions.body: Runs are triggered from /ops, never executed by the app. The flow is: click Run -> a server action dispatches the harvest workflow with dry_run=true and a generated dispatch_id echoed into the run-name for correlation -> the app polls (every 5s, up to ~60s) for the run and downloads its quote.json artifact -> it displays the quote (calls, records, duration, estimated_usd) plus a budget snapshot (month-to-date, caps, remaining, would_exceed) -> the operator confirms -> a second dispatch runs the real harvest. The quote is DETERMINISTIC and makes zero harvest API calls: tools/run-connector.ts gains a `quote` subcommand backed by an optional connector.quote(params) method (evidence estimates from the record's evidence_terms, pins, per-term caps, and the 1s polite interval) and merges a budget snapshot from tools/ops-gate.ts. If the quote exceeds remaining budget, confirmation is blocked until the operator ticks an explicit 'raise cap for this run' checkbox; ticking it makes the server action append a decisions.json auto-entry recording the override before the real dispatch, and passes raise_cap=true to the workflow (which bypasses ONLY the budget gate, never the per-run limits). Quotes are ephemeral estimates, not knowledge — they return as a run artifact and are never committed, so quote spam cannot bury meaningful data in git history. Polling is bounded: if the quote is not ready within ~60s the UI stops and shows 'quote pending — check the run' with a link to the Actions run, never hanging. The scheduled fleet run reuses the same tools/ops-gate.ts gate (paused, cadence-due, per-run limits against the estimate, and budget) and writes every skip reason to the job summary; the D-022 retry-then-issue automation is reused verbatim for real runs.

decisions.title: Connection means "set up", not "last run succeeded" — run quality becomes its own computed axis alongside health
decisions.body: The owner's reading of the /sources board is: connection answers "have we already set up this source" (we have 35 sources — the board must show which ones are wired), a second signal answers "is it working well", and health (D-021) answers "is the API accessible right now". The old rule conflated the first two: connected required a manifest listing the source with last_run.status "success", so one partial run (e.g. the keyless S2 429 harvest, D-020) flipped an already-set-up source to not_connected — set-up state and run quality fought over one pill. Redefinition in lib/status.ts computeSourceState: an api/internal source is connected iff ANY /corpora/{dir}/manifest.json lists it in source_ids, regardless of run status — a manifest only exists after a connector was built and run at least once, so its presence IS the file-based set-up proof (a connector merely registered in code but never run stays not_connected, because nothing on disk can prove it). A report source is ingested iff a manifest lists it AND a data_files entry exists on disk (the success requirement dropped for the same reason — the artifact is either on disk or not). New axis: computeSourceLastRun returns the newest last_run (status/timestamp/corpus) across manifests listing the source, rendered through the existing RUN_STATUS_META (success emerald / partial amber / failed red) as a "last run" column on /sources and /connectors; granularity stays per corpus (D-020) — all sources one corpus harvests share its run status, and per-source run granularity remains the future D-014/D-020 refinement. Health is untouched. Effect on current data: openalex and semantic-scholar render connected + last run partial + health degraded (truthful: set up, last harvest throttled, currently throttled); wayback-cdx and pubmed-europepmc render not_connected + no run + health ok (truthful: API fine, connector not built); the overview mode count becomes 2/7 connected. No schema or validator change — manifests are untouched and everything is recomputed at render time. Docs rewritten to the three-axis rule: SPEC §4, sources/README, corpora/README, and the tools/README runbook matrix (connection × last run × health).

decisions.title: Semantic Scholar rate compliance — one global 1 rps queue per process, 2s backoff on residual 429s, fetch-layer enforcement of the _ops run budget, workflow-level concurrency group
decisions.body: The issued Semantic Scholar key allows 1 request/second CUMULATIVE across ALL endpoints — search, paper details, references, and health probes draw from one allowance, so per-endpoint pacing is non-compliant by construction. Compliance is enforced structurally in the shared fetch layer, not by connector discipline. (1) Global queue: tools/connectors/lib/http.ts gains enqueueS2(), a single per-process promise chain that serializes every request to api.semanticscholar.org at ≥1100ms spacing (the 100ms margin absorbs clock skew against S2’s rate counter); createPoliteFetch routes S2 URLs through the queue automatically, and tools/health-check.ts routes its S2 probe through the same queue — S2 calls are never parallelized, and the rule for future tools is: no S2 call outside createPoliteFetch or enqueueS2(). (2) Residual 429s: a 429 despite the limiter retries with exponential backoff starting at 2s (2s, 4s; other hosts stay at 1s, 2s; Retry-After still wins when present) and the evidence connector records warnings: { s2_throttled: true } on ANY S2 429 — keyed or keyless — while the keyless per-term batch reduction from D-018 stays keyless-only. (3) Run budgets: the runner reads the connector’s /corpora/_ops/connectors/{id}.json (contract D-024, shared loaders in lib/ops.ts) and passes limits.max_calls_per_run into createPoliteFetch, which fails the next request once the budget (retries included) is spent — the D-025 pre-run quote ceiling is thereby also enforced DURING the run at the fetch layer, and a connector cannot opt out. The evidence default drops from 500 to 150: sized so the worst case (every call S2) stays under ~3 minutes at 1 rps; a normal run uses ~25–50 calls. Reference snowballing deliberately stays on OpenAlex only: it carries the same citation graph without the 1 rps ceiling, so reference expansion never spends S2 budget. (4) Cross-process concurrency: .github/workflows/connectors.yml previously had NO concurrency group — verified, not assumed — and gains a workflow-level group connectors-s2 (cancel-in-progress false) covering every job in the file, the health heartbeat today and any future scheduled harvest job; any connector workflow living in a separate file (e.g. harvest.yml) must reuse the exact group name so two runner processes never call S2 simultaneously. Within one job the heartbeat’s S2 probe and any connector S2 calls share the process queue; as separate scheduled jobs they now queue behind each other instead of colliding. (5) Runbook (tools/README.md): S2 = 1 rps cumulative per key; do not add S2 calls to any new tool without routing through the shared limiter. Evidence connector bumped to 2.1.0.

decisions.title: Connector #2 (wayback) — quarterly Wayback CDX capture index per survivor domain; URLs and dates only, no page contents
decisions.body: The interfaces corpus starts as a time-lapse INDEX of surviving products' web surfaces, not a content archive. tools/connectors/wayback.ts (sourceId wayback, source_ids [wayback-cdx]) makes ONE CDX API call per domain — /cdx/search/cdx with output=json, from/to year bounds (default 2015-2026), filter=statuscode:200, collapse=timestamp:6, fl=timestamp,original — and reduces client-side to the FIRST capture of each quarter (CDX collapse can express months via the YYYYMM timestamp prefix but not quarters, so the server collapses to ≤1/month and the connector keeps ≤4/year). Output: /corpora/wayback/{domain}.json { domain, path, fetched_at, years, captures[]: { date, wayback_url, original_url } }. Page contents are DELIBERATELY not downloaded at this step — a full-page corpus would blow the 40 MB corpus guardrail immediately; content harvesting is a later, size-conscious step against this index. The domain list is owner-editable DATA, not code: tools/connectors/wayback-domains.json ships with 10 survivors (duolingo.com, calm.com, notion.so, canva.com, headspace.com, strava.com, grammarly.com, dropbox.com, spotify.com, blinkist.com); a domains="a.com;b.com" param overrides for ad-hoc runs, path=/onboarding scopes the query to a sub-surface, years=YYYY-YYYY bounds the range. Failure handling mirrors evidence.ts: a failing domain is logged and skipped (run status partial with joined errors), the run throws only when every domain failed, and a domain with zero archived captures still writes an honest empty index — the archive having nothing is a finding, not an error. Ops config corpora/_ops/connectors/wayback.json: cadence 90 days, max_calls_per_run 40, max_records_per_run 2000, and targets [] DELIBERATELY — the D-024 target machinery is mechanism-centric (targets validate against registry mechanism ids and freshness reads registry git history), while domains are connector data in wayback-domains.json; scheduled runs therefore skip with the honest "no targets configured" reason and harvests are triggered manually or from /ops (blank target dispatches the full list). Wiring domains into the scheduler is a separate future decision. quote() (D-025) is deterministic: calls = domains, records = domains × years × 4 quarters (upper bound), duration ≈ calls × 1s polite interval, estimated_usd 0 (CDX is free, D-011).

decisions.title: Report ingest tool — tools/ingest-report.ts normalizes owner-prepared benchmark tables into the /corpora/benchmarks corpus; report sources need a normalizer, not a connector
decisions.body: Report-mode sources (connection_mode "report", D-013 — revenuecat-report, unbounce-benchmarks, goodui, product-analytics-benchmarks, forrt) live in published PDFs a human downloads and reads: there is nothing for a connector to fetch (the D-011 whitelist does not cover them, and gated report PDFs are not scrapable — rule 12). The other half of the pipeline is a NORMALIZER: the owner prepares a small table, the tool structures and validates it. tools/ingest-report.ts (npm run ingest -- <source_id> <file.(csv|json|md)> [retrieved=YYYY-MM-DD]) validates that <source_id> exists in sources.json AND is connection_mode "report", parses the input by extension (.csv with a header row and a quote-aware splitter, .json as an array of row objects, .md as the first GitHub-flavored pipe table), normalizes every row to { metric, category?, value, unit, notes? } with minimal shape validation (metric/unit non-empty strings, value a finite number, category/notes optional), and — one bad row aborts the whole run BEFORE any write, a benchmark corpus is whole or not written — writes /corpora/benchmarks/{source_id}.json = { source_id, retrieved, metrics[] }. It then writes/merges /corpora/benchmarks/manifest.json (corpus id "benchmarks") whose source_ids accumulate every ingested report source (D-014: one corpus, several sources; re-ingest is idempotent). The tool makes ZERO network calls (cost.api_calls 0, estimated_usd 0) and touches ONLY /corpora/benchmarks — sources.json stays git-only and statuses stay COMPUTED (D-013/D-023/D-026): computeSourceState flips a report source to "ingested" iff a manifest lists it in source_ids AND its data file exists on disk, so ingesting the file IS the status change, nothing is hardcoded. Contract safety mirrors D-020/D-021/D-024: the writer type (BenchmarkFile/BenchmarkMetric in tools/ingest-report.ts) and reader mirror (lib/types.ts) are pinned by an AssertAssignable drift guard in tools/validate.ts, which also validates every /corpora/benchmarks/*.json against the record schema and requires the filename stem to be a report-mode source id. writeManifest was refactored to take a ManifestIdentity ({ sourceId, sourceIds, connectorVersion }) instead of a full Connector so the ingester (which is not a connector) and the connector runner share one manifest writer. Content rule 8 holds: the tool writes code and structure, never numbers — benchmark values come only from the owner's real report extracts. First targets: RevenueCat State of Subscription Apps (trial->paid CVR and retention by app category), Unbounce conversion benchmarks (landing CVR by industry), GoodUI (pattern test win/loss outcomes); the benchmarks corpus backs the future effects table's baseline column.

decisions.title: Scheduled orchestration consolidated in connectors.yml — heartbeat 6h / evidence weekly / wayback monthly, health-aware skipping, per-connector auto-commit; harvest.yml becomes dispatch-only
decisions.body: Step 6 assembles the final scheduled surface without rebuilding the gate. connectors.yml now owns EVERY scheduled connector job and carries three cron entries routed by github.event.schedule: 0 */6 * * * (heartbeat, D-021, unchanged, also workflow_dispatch), 0 5 * * 1 (evidence weekly), 0 6 1 * * (wayback monthly, 1st 06:00 UTC). The weekly scheduled job was MOVED out of harvest.yml, which is now dispatch-only (quote + confirmed run from /ops, D-025); its schedule trigger and scheduled job were deleted and the header rewritten. Both files keep the workflow-level concurrency group connectors-s2 (cancel-in-progress false, D-027), so the monthly wayback run colliding with the 06:00 heartbeat tick on the 1st serializes instead of racing S2, and manual dispatches are covered by the same guarantee. A new generic harvest-scheduled job is parameterized by CONNECTOR_ID (picked from the schedule: wayback on the monthly cron, else evidence) and reuses the existing patterns verbatim — fetch-depth 0 for the freshness git log, ops-gate plan for the decision, the D-022 retry-once-then-deduplicated-issue automation, and honest 'commit only when git sees a diff'. Every scheduled path already respects paused (with reason), per-run limits (pre-run quote gate + fetch-layer enforcement, D-027), the monthly budget (skip with a logged 'gate blocked' reason, raise_cap never passed on the schedule), and the S2 global queue — verified wired for scheduled context in tools/ops-gate.ts plan (which only the scheduled jobs call), NOT duplicated. Three additions to the gate, no rewrite: (1) plan takes an optional connectorId so each schedule plans only its own connector; (2) HEALTH-AWARE SKIP — planForConnector reads /corpora/_health/heartbeat.json and, if any source the connector harvests (connector.sourceIds) is status 'down' within the HEARTBEAT_STALE_HOURS window (12h, reusing lib/status.ts), skips the whole connector with reason 'source {id} down at HH:MM' (UTC) instead of hammering a dead API into a red run; a missing/stale heartbeat never claims down (the run proceeds and its own retry/issue automation handles a real outage) and 'degraded' does not skip (connectors degrade gracefully on S2 429s, D-027); (3) WAYBACK SCHEDULABILITY — the mechanism-centric target machinery (targets validate against registry mechanism ids and freshness reads registry git history) does not fit wayback, whose scope is the owner-editable wayback-domains.json (D-028). Rather than force fake targets, the Connector contract gains an optional schedulableWithoutTargets flag (set on waybackConnector); when true and _ops targets is empty, plan emits a single default-scope entry (target null, params {}) that still passes cadence, health, and the quote/budget gate — every other connector keeps the honest 'no targets configured' skip. wayback keeps _ops cadence.every_days 90, so the monthly schedule is the CEILING and ops-gate still honestly skips 'not due' until 90 days elapse, matching the quarterly-index design (D-028). Auto-commit for scheduled harvests changed from the flat 'data: scheduled harvest' to 'data(connector): {id} run {YYYY-MM-DD}' so the git log names which connector produced each change. Job summary per run appends the plan's skipped-with-reasons list plus the connector manifest last_run stats (status, records, calls, duration_s, estimated_usd), guarded by a 'ran' output so a nothing-due week never reports a stale manifest as this run. No schema or validator change: the gate reuses existing shared loaders, statuses stay COMPUTED, and the heartbeat/manifests are untouched.

decisions.title: The /docs library gains an operator runbook — docs/connectors-runbook.md, rendered alongside the five foundation documents
decisions.body: Step 8 adds docs/connectors-runbook.md: a plain-language operator's manual for the source-connector fleet, written for a non-technical owner and the August team. It documents the two harvest paths (schedule via connectors.yml; the /ops Run button with dry-run quote confirmation via harvest.yml, D-025) and explicitly separates harvesting from guarding — push CI (validate.yml) validates knowledge and manifests but never fetches, so the earlier 'three ways runs happen' framing is corrected to two harvest paths plus a guard layer. It also covers the connection-vs-health status axes and their four combinations (D-021/D-026), the budget model and logged cap-override flow (D-023/D-024/D-025), the per-source cadence table and the S2 1-rps cumulative shared-queue rule with OpenAlex-only snowballing (D-027), the evidence corpus rules including the dissent gate (D-015/D-017/D-019), the 40 MB Postgres-escalation guardrail and no-raw-HTML rule (D-028), the retry-once-then-deduplicated-issue failure policy and 'watch issues, not logs' contract (D-022), the ordered checklist for adding a new connector, and the licensing rule that connection_mode manual sources are never machine-harvested. Wiring: DOC_SLUGS in lib/data.ts gains 'connectors-runbook' so it renders at /docs/connectors-runbook via the existing app/docs/[slug] route with zero new code — operators read it inside the app. This extends the /docs set beyond the SPEC §3.6 foundation five; the distinction is preserved in the code comment and docs/README (the first five are the owner-authored foundation set, the runbook is an operational manual maintained alongside the ops layer). No schema, validator, or content-rule change: the file is owner/ops Markdown like every other /docs file, and the app still only renders docs, never edits them (rule 1). Every quantitative claim in the runbook (monthly caps $5/20000, per-run limits 150/40, cadences 7d/90d, 12h heartbeat staleness, 40 MB guardrail, 1100ms S2 spacing) is copied from and labelled with the config/code file that owns it, so the runbook cites the source of truth rather than becoming a second one.

decisions.title: First dossier (DOS-LA-01, incubating) + dossier schema carries prose — per-axis markdown rationale, a dissent statement, and a core_condition inside the JSON (Option A, one projection)
decisions.body: The first admission-gate dossier lands for LA-01, and the dossier contract is extended so the scientific reasoning lives IN the record rather than being discarded. Option A (one source, projections) is chosen over building a separate markdown pipeline (rejected B/C): JSON stays the single source of truth and /dossiers renders it — no second file type, no md loader/route to maintain for one record kind. Schema changes in dossiers/dossier.schema.json: (1) each of the five scoring axes changes from a bare integer to an object { score: int 0–3, rationale: markdown string } via a new $defs.axis, so the owner's justification for every score is part of the record; (2) a top-level dissent: markdown string is REQUIRED — every dossier must state its counter-evidence, mirroring the D-019 evidence-corpus dissent gate at the decision layer; (3) a top-level core_condition: string states the measured condition for promotion to CORE (measured, not assumed); (4) evidence_sources changes from string[] to { ref, doi? }[] so citations carry resolvable DOIs. The reader mirror (lib/types.ts: DossierAxis, DossierEvidenceSource, updated DossierScores/Dossier) and the validator follow: tools/validate.ts now sums scores[*].score (not the axis objects) for the total-equals-sum check; the D-019 checkDossierDissent gate (referenced evidence corpus must exist, be classified, and have a non-empty dissent category) is unchanged and satisfied by /corpora/evidence/LA-01.json (dissent category count 26). The /dossiers page renders the rationales and dissent through the existing react-markdown + remark-gfm pipeline already used by /docs (no new dependency, rule against future deps honored), plus a DOI-linked sources list; the empty-state copy is de-staled since a dossier now exists. dossiers/LA-01.json is owner-approved content committed verbatim (DOS-LA-01, verdict incubating, total 13, evidence 3 / product_applicability 3 / measurability 3 / orthogonality 2 / safety 2 — clears total ≥ 11, evidence ≥ 2, safety ≥ 2); code did not author any score, rationale, or claim (rule 8). The registry record registry/mechanisms/LA-01.json sets dossier_ref: "dossiers/LA-01.json" (was null). Statuses stay COMPUTED: lifecycle_status was already 'incubating' and the dossier now backs it; promotion to CORE remains blocked on core_condition (a recorded measured effect), never hardcoded.

decisions.title: Batch 1 harvest prep — seed sub-schema widened for owner evidence_terms/pinned_evidence, EN-03/VR-02/ZE-07 added to evidence targets, and a pin_unresolved output flag so a dead pinned DOI is a finding, not a run failure
decisions.body: Preparing the first multi-mechanism evidence harvest (Batch 1) required three small, aligned changes and no new machinery. (1) SCHEMA: registry/mechanism.schema.json $defs.seedStub gains two OPTIONAL properties — evidence_terms (array of non-empty strings) and pinned_evidence ({ title, doi, reason }[], additionalProperties false) — reusing the exact shapes the full L1 record already defines. The stub stays closed (additionalProperties false) and stays a stub: neither field is added to required, id/name/grade_draft/oneliner/parent/lifecycle_status are untouched, and rule 8/9 holds — a candidate can now be HARVESTED before it is fleshed out without inventing any mechanism content. The evidence connector already read both fields from seed stubs (loadMechanism falls back to _seed/{id}.json; MechanismRecord already declared them), so only the validator's seedStub gate was blocking owner-provided terms/pins on a stub. (2) DATA: EN-03, VR-02, ZE-07 seed stubs receive owner-provided evidence_terms and pinned_evidence verbatim (endowment effect, variable reward, progress/incompleteness respectively — each pin set includes a dissent/boundary entry per D-015/D-019 intent), and corpora/_ops/connectors/evidence.json targets grows from [LA-01] to [LA-01, EN-03, VR-02, ZE-07]. validateOpsConnectorConfig checks each target against the registry roster (seed ids included), and each per-run quote stays well under the config max_calls_per_run 150 (EN-03 heaviest at ~17 calls). (3) BEHAVIOR: tools/connectors/evidence.ts fetchPinnedWork now sets pin_unresolved: true on the fallback record returned when a pinned DOI does not resolve on OpenAlex (both the null-record and catch paths). The run already never threw for a failed pin — the pin entered the corpus with owner-provided metadata — this only makes the failure VISIBLE in the output so the owner can correct the DOI; a resolved pin (success path) carries no flag, and a pin overlapping a harvested search record stays unmarked. pin_unresolved is an additive optional field on EvidenceRecord, so no reader contract breaks. No harvest is triggered here — this is prep only; owner/ops triggers the actual runs.
